body.statement: For every \(B\in\mathcal B_G\), the law \(P^B\) from def:gaussian-completion has observed margin exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), including every cross-setting covariance, satisfies the partially linear model, has \(B(P^B)=B\), belongs to \(\mathcal M_G(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{HK}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and yields \(\theta(P^B)=s-B\). Coordinatewise, if \(B_i\ne0\), then \((s_i-B_i)D_i+B_i(D_i+U_i/B_i)=s_iD_i+U_i=Y_i\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(D_i\mid X,A_i^B)=\operatorname{Var}(U_i)/(B_i^2+\operatorname{Var}(U_i))>0\); if \(B_i=0\), then \(s_iD_i+U_i=Y_i\), \(E[U_i\mid D_i,X,Z_i]=0\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(D_i\mid X,Z_i)=1\).
body.justification: A sharpness claim needs one observationally equivalent latent-confounder completion for every feasible bias vector.
body.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026 proves containment algebraically and gives no reverse construction; BalkePearl1997 supplies the methodological standard for attainment but not this model.
body.consumer: It makes the union sharp over a nondegenerate jointly Gaussian observed-law family while preserving arbitrary observed dependence across settings.
